tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded session demonstrates logging into Magento admin and interacting with the Manage Products grid (filters, Search, Reset), using mass-action controls, opening product edit pages, and creating a new product. The recorded run captured stable element hashes for login controls, grid filters, the Search/Reset buttons, Add Product controls, mass-action controls, and per-row Edit links.

Task Definition:
- Build a deterministic, re-usable tool that: navigates to the Magento Admin Products grid, applies a comprehensive set of filters supplied by the user (sku, name, price/qty ranges, type, attribute set, visibility, status, website, store view), executes Search, then opens a product Edit page (either direct by product_id or by clicking the first row Edit link). Finally extract the edit page content for verification.

Action Plan:
1) Navigate to the Manage Products grid URL.
2) Populate every filter control recorded in the session using stable element hashes (inputs/selects). All filters are parameterized so an empty parameter corresponds to leaving a filter blank.
3) Click the Search button to apply filters and wait for the grid to refresh.
4) Attempt a direct navigation to the product Edit URL when product_id is provided (fast path).
5) Click the first-row Edit link as a reliable UI fallback to open an edit page when product_id is not used.
6) Extract the edit page content for verification.

Variable Identification (inputs required):
- admin_base_url (required): base admin URL used to build navigation targets.
- product_id (optional): if provided tool will attempt direct navigation to edit URL.
- sku, name, price_from, price_to, qty_from, qty_to, type, attribute_set_id, visibility, status, website, store_view: all optional filters used to narrow search results.
- open_first_match (bool): user preference to click the first result (tool uses a click to open first row; parameter left for caller to control usage in their orchestration).

Step Optimization and Notes:
- Where available the recorded element_hash values are used to make interaction deterministic. These element hashes target the exact elements the recording used (Search: 99366bc9df; SKU filter: f127a4b0da; Price/Qty: 8e38c5e838, 927c2c13e5, 0a91de9a0e, bdecbf7d2c; Type/Attrib/Visibility/Status/Website selects: 59a067e4b4, 97d647bb6f, fef9e4ddbc, 2d0526510b, b0f990d697; first-row Edit link: 324bf9fa77). Using these avoids brittle text/XPath matching.
- The tool prefers direct navigation to the Edit URL when product_id is available (faster, avoids needing the row to be visible), but still clicks the Edit link as a UI fallback to cover more cases.
- The tool intentionally writes to every filter control deterministically (empty values leave filters effectively unchanged) to avoid branching logic in the step sequence while still respecting optional inputs.
- Authentication is not included (the recording assumed an authenticated session). If the environment presents a login screen, callers must authenticate before running this tool or modify the tool to include login steps.

Limitations and Safety:
- Mass actions and destructive operations are intentionally excluded from this tool. The recorded session showed massaction patterns; if mass operations are required they should be implemented in a separate, explicitly-confirmed tool that enumerates option values and requires explicit confirmation.
- Some admin UI behaviors rely on JavaScript (AJAX filtering, dynamic option rendering). The tool works against the recorded selectors; callers should run it in a JS-enabled browser/context to ensure full functionality.

This tool design follows the recorded actions, uses stable element hashes for deterministic interactions, and provides a reproducible flow for searching and opening a product for editing.
name: magento_admin_find_and_open_product
description: Automates searching the Magento Admin Products grid with multiple filters (sku, name, id, price range, qty range, type, attribute set, visibility, status, website) and opens a product for editing. Uses recorded stable element hashes from the session when available.

steps.description: Open the Manage Products grid (Products list) in the admin.
Enter SKU into the SKU filter input (recorded element hash from session). Leave empty string if not filtering by SKU.
Enter Price 'From' value into the Price-from filter input (recorded element hash).
Enter Price 'To' value into the Price-to filter input (recorded element hash).
Enter Qty 'From' value into the Qty-from filter input (recorded element hash).
Enter Qty 'To' value into the Qty-to filter input (recorded element hash).
Select the product Type filter (recorded element hash). Provide visible option text (e.g. 'Simple Product'). If blank, the selection is left as-is.
Select the Attribute Set filter (recorded element hash). Provide visible option text (e.g. 'Default').
Enter Name filter value into the Name filter input (recorded element hash used earlier when selecting a row).
Select Visibility filter option (recorded element hash). Provide visible option text.
Select Status filter option (recorded element hash). Provide visible option text (Enabled/Disabled).
Select Website filter option (recorded element hash). Provide visible option text (e.g. 'Main Website').
Set the Choose Store View selector. Use visible text such as 'All Store Views'.
Click the Search (Apply Filters) button to run the grid filter.
Wait for the grid to refresh after applying filters.
If product_id was provided this attempts a direct navigation to the product Edit page (fast path). If product_id is empty this navigation will not locate an item and is harmless in many setups.
Click the first row 'Edit' link (recorded element hash). This opens the first matched product for editing if present on the page.
Extract the Product Edit page content (Save/Back selectors and key product fields) for validation and downstream automation.

input_schema.name: product_id
input_schema.description: Product ID to open directly for editing (when provided the tool will try the direct edit URL).

input_schema.name: sku
input_schema.description: SKU filter value to enter into the SKU column filter (exact or partial).

input_schema.name: name
input_schema.description: Name filter value to enter into the Name column filter (exact or partial).

input_schema.name: price_from
input_schema.description: Price FROM value for the Price range filter (numeric string).

input_schema.name: price_to
input_schema.description: Price TO value for the Price range filter (numeric string).

input_schema.name: qty_from
input_schema.description: Quantity FROM value for the Qty range filter (numeric string).

input_schema.name: qty_to
input_schema.description: Quantity TO value for the Qty range filter (numeric string).

input_schema.name: type
input_schema.description: Product type to select in the Type filter (e.g. 'Simple Product', 'Configurable Product', ...). Use visible option text exactly as shown in the admin.

input_schema.name: attribute_set_id
input_schema.description: Attribute set visible text (e.g. 'Default') to select in the filter; pass the visible option text.

input_schema.name: visibility
input_schema.description: Visibility filter value (visible option text e.g. 'Catalog, Search').

input_schema.name: status
input_schema.description: Status filter value (visible option text 'Enabled' or 'Disabled').

input_schema.name: website
input_schema.description: Website filter visible option text (e.g. 'Main Website').

input_schema.name: store_view
input_schema.description: Store view to set in the 'Choose Store View' selector (e.g. 'All Store Views'). If empty, leaves current store view as-is.

input_schema.name: open_first_match
input_schema.description: If true (default) the tool clicks the first row's Edit link after filtering. If false, the tool will not click the Edit link (useful if you only want to search).
